h1:
Rayong Aquarium
A Cheap Indoor Stop That Kids Love
intro: When the weather turns or you just want a cool, easy spot to keep the kids happy, the Rayong Aquarium in Ban Phe is the answer plenty of families forget about. Tickets are just a few baht, there's an underwater glass tunnel to walk through, a touch pool where kids can hold a starfish, and it sits right next to Ban Phe market — so you can carry on for seafood or hop a boat to Koh Samet straight after.
chips: 💸 A few baht to get in

blocks.html: The full name here is the Rayong Aquarium, and a lot of people just call it the Rayong fish museum. The building sits inside the Eastern Marine Fisheries Research and Development Center in Phe sub-district, near Ban Phe market and the pier for Koh Samet — which makes it a natural stop to fold into a Rayong beach trip. It isn't a big, flashy mall-style aquarium; it's a learning center run by the Fisheries Department, focused on marine life from the Gulf of Thailand. Families come to walk through at an easy pace, and it doesn't take long.

The walkway is laid out in zones, starting with shallow-water tanks and working through to coral tanks and the commercial fish of the Gulf. The bit that gets the loudest reaction from kids is the glass tunnel you walk under the big tank, with fish swimming right over your head.

items: Underwater glass tunnel — a big tank you walk beneath, with schools of fish swimming all around you. It's the photo spot kids love most.
Touch pool — a shallow pool where kids can try holding a starfish, sea cucumber, and other soft-bodied sea creatures, with staff keeping an eye on things.
Coral and clownfish tanks — a bright, colorful zone where kids will point and ask the names of every fish.
Sea turtle pool — sea turtles to watch up close, with signs explaining the conservation work.
Seashell and fishing-gear museum zone — telling the story of the fishing trade and the marine resources of the eastern coast.

blocks.title: Bringing little ones
blocks.html: Kids under 120 cm get in free, and the touch pool is the highlight for the preschool crowd. Bring a hand towel along — hands will definitely be wet after holding a starfish.

blocks.html: The price is genuinely cheap compared with most indoor attractions. The one thing to lock in your memory: it's closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. Plenty of people drive all the way to the gate and find a closed sign, so check the day before you set off.

items: Free entry: kids under 120 cm tall and seniors aged 60 and over

blocks.title: How long it takes
blocks.html: At an easy pace it's about 45 minutes to an hour to see everything. It's a short stop you can pair with Ban Phe market or a boat over to Koh Samet on the same day — no need to block out the whole day for it.

The building is inside the research center grounds in Phe sub-district, about 20 km from Rayong town — roughly a 30-minute drive. If you're coming from the Ban Phe pier it's just a little further on. There's a parking lot inside the center, so you can park there with no separate parking fee.

items.name: Ban Phe Market
items.blurb: The souvenir and fresh-seafood market is right nearby — walk over for dried shrimp and fish sauce, or sit down for a seafood meal.

items.name: Koh Samet Pier
items.blurb: Catch a boat across to Koh Samet from Ban Phe. It works well to hit the aquarium in the morning, then carry on to the island by boat.

items.name: Rayong Food
items.blurb: A Ban Phe trip pairs easily with seafood and local Rayong eats.

blocks.html: Don't expect it to be as big or eye-popping as a Bangkok mall aquarium. This is a Fisheries Department learning center — compact in scale, and a few of the tank signs are getting old. But in exchange for a ticket of just a few baht and an uncrowded feel, it's great value for bringing kids to see real sea creatures up close. The draw here is the price and a location that slots into a beach trip — not spectacle.

blocks.title: Best days to skip the crowds
blocks.html: Weekdays (Wed–Fri) are far quieter than weekends, so kids get the touch pool to themselves without jostling. If you can avoid it, steer clear of long holiday weekends when it gets packed.

faq.q: What days is Rayong Aquarium open?
faq.a: It's open Wednesday to Friday 10:00–16:00, and Saturday–Sunday plus public holidays 10:00–17:00. It's closed on Monday and Tuesday. Check the day before you set off, since plenty of people arrive to find the gate closed.
Adults 30 THB, children under 15 are 10 THB, and kids under 120 cm tall plus seniors aged 60 and over get in free. That's very cheap for an indoor attraction.

Very much so. The highlights are the underwater glass tunnel and the touch pool, where kids can try holding a starfish and other soft-bodied sea creatures. Walking through takes about 45 minutes to an hour — not too long for little ones.

faq.q: Where is it, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's inside the Eastern Marine Fisheries Research and Development Center in Phe sub-district, near Ban Phe market and the Koh Samet pier. You can walk over for seafood at Ban Phe market, or catch a boat to Koh Samet the same day.

faq.q: How long does a visit take?
faq.a: At an easy pace it's about 45 minutes to an hour to cover every zone. It's a short stop that pairs nicely with a Ban Phe or Koh Samet trip.
